body.title: Apply retained-target and guard rules to the control script
body.summary: Update existing shell stop/wait/force-stop/restart functions to use the same identity/ownership contract, reusing shared Node helpers through a minimal internal executable if needed rather than duplicating weaker PID logic. Retain original target, verify before kill, preserve replacement files and surface unrecovered guard errors. Keep existing script user-facing commands. Remove cmd_restart's cmd_stop || true suppression. Explicitly return nonzero from cmd_start and cmd_restart on stop, capability or ownership failure before spawn_daemon, including shell conditional contexts.
acceptanceChecks: Script waits or forces the captured process after PID/socket deletion.
Reused PID, replacement files, missing helper/identity and orphan guard never trigger unsafe kill or successful restart.
Disposable shell integration proves clean and forced-stop outcomes without touching the installed daemon.
Both cmd_start and cmd_restart propagate every relevant failure before spawn_daemon; no reliance on errexit inside conditional/OR contexts.

tests.name: Control script retains the original target across run-file removal
Control script refuses reused identity, replacement files and orphan guards
Disposable clean and forced script restart paths preserve commands
Shell start and restart refuse spawn after lifecycle failures even in conditional contexts
